newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa minister's in-law worked for apartheid.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa minister's in-law worked for apartheid.

text.p: While Joe Modise, now South Africa's defence minister, was leading the armed struggle against apartheid, he had a traitor in his own close family, the truth commission heard on Tuesday.

Glory Sedibe was a member of the African National Congress's military unit Umkhonto we Sizwe (Spear of the Nation), which his brother-in-law Modise led, until Sedibe was abducted from a jail in Swaziland in 1986 by an undercover apartheid police unit.
One former policeman who helped abduct him, Butana Almond Nofomela, told the truth commission that Sedibe had then been coerced into working as an agent of the white-led government.
The revelation that Modise's own brother-in-law, who has since died of a heart attack, worked for the hated apartheid rulers came as a complete surprise to many South Africans.
It was unclear from Nofomela's brief testimony at his amnesty hearing in Johannesburg what military secrets of the ANC's armed wing were passed to the government by Sedibe.

Nofomela, who was a policeman in a now notorious apartheid dirty-tricks unit, is asking for amnesty for the abduction and 15 other crimes listed by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission as gross human rights violations.
Jackie Sedibe -- Glory Sedibe's sister and Modise's wife -- is now an army general in a unit leading the transformation of the old white-led army into a fully integrated military force.

Nofomela said the unit that abducted Sedibe was led by police colonel Eugene de Kock, sentenced in October to 200 years in jail for six murders and a host of other offences carried out in a campaign to crush apartheid's black opponents.
